Jess L: Hey team — HR announced a carrier change effective 2026-06-01. Can I add my domestic partner retro to 2026-05-15? Partner was covered on their employer plan until 2026-05-20. What proof do you need?
Maria (People Ops): Hi Jess — a company-initiated carrier transition qualifies for a special enrollment window. We typically allow a 60-day window for enrollments tied to an employer carrier swap. Please upload proof of prior coverage termination (or letter from their employer) plus a domestic partnership affidavit or marriage certificate. Submit everything through the benefits portal.
Sam (Benefits): Also note: we need the completed dependent enrollment form, dependent SSN if available (or passport + alternate tax forms if not). If the prior plan terminated after 5/20 we'll base retro calculations on the carrier effective date, not before the administrative cutoff. We'll also need a payroll ticket to process any retro adjustments.
Jess L: Partner is a Canadian citizen and doesn't have a US SSN. What IDs are acceptable?
Maria (People Ops): Passport + proof of residency + the signed Dependent Affidavit (we have a template in the portal) are acceptable for enrollment. For tax and imputed income purposes, Finance will evaluate whether the partner qualifies as a tax dependent.
Finance: Correct — if the partner is not claimed as a tax dependent we will treat employer-paid premium portion as imputed income. We'll calculate imputed income starting on the coverage effective date and process through payroll. Expect the imputed income and any retro adjustments to appear within one payroll cycle after Benefits submits the ticket.
PayrollBot: Retro deduction request received: ticket #PR-2026-441. Processing ETA: next two payroll runs.
Sam (Benefits): Practical steps: 1) Upload passport + employer termination letter to https://benefits.redwood.com/portal, 2) complete and sign the dependent enrollment form, 3) sign the domestic partnership affidavit, 4) reply here after upload so we can open the payroll ticket.
Jess L: Done — I uploaded passport, employer termination letter, and signed affidavit on 2026-06-10 in the portal. @Sam can you confirm which effective date the premiums will use?
Sam (Benefits): Confirmed — the coverage will be effective 2026-06-01 (carrier effective date). We cannot backdate enrollment to 2026-05-15 due to the carrier admin cutoff. Retro premiums will be pro-rated starting 6/01 and payroll will apply the retro debit on the next reconciliation run.
Maria (People Ops): Thanks all — I approved the QLE in the benefits system and flagged the payroll ticket for priority processing. Jess, expect a confirmation email and new benefits card in ~7–10 business days. :party_parrot:
